detail: rca.verified == true, confidence 0.97, no prior remediation object on the incident. Gate passes, so a fix proposal is permitted. Read personality.md and the capability's own playbooks/patch-proposal-technique.md first (experiences/ is empty - no prior fix to recall).

curl raw.githubusercontent.com/.../src/product-catalog/main.go. Read GetProduct and checkProductFailure first-hand rather than trusting the RCA summary. Confirmed L373 call, L374 literal msg, L377 status.Error(codes.Internal, msg), L380 getProductFromDB reached only if branch not taken, L419-420 flags.ProductCatalogFailure.Value with NewTargetlessEvaluationContext.
finding: The code has no defect. It reads a flag and, when true, does exactly what the flag exists to make it do - including the span status and span event that made this incident diagnosable at all.

detail: Chose config_proposal over code_fix, against the surface reading of the type rule (RCA names a real file and function, which points at code_fix).
reasoning: Every patch available to main.go was either symptom-hiding (delete/bypass the flag check, or add a fallback - 'an error caught and silently ignored is not a fix, it's the same failure with the evidence removed') or configurability-destroying (hardcode the flag false - 'preserve configurability, don't hardcode around it'). Both are named anti-patterns in my own playbook. When every available patch is bad, the change doesn't belong in that file. The cause of the incident is not that the branch exists; it's that the flag evaluated true at runtime, and configuration is where that fix lives.

detail: gh api .../contents/src/flagd located demo.flagd.json (did not assume the path); curl read it. Committed productCatalogFailure is defaultVariant 'off', state ENABLED, variants {off:false,on:true}, targeting if(product_id == OLJCESPC7Z) then 'off' else 'off'.
finding: The committed config is already correct in every branch. There is no bad default checked in anywhere to fix - this is runtime drift, and drift is not fixed by a commit.
counterfactual: Before this fetch the obvious move was 'PR a change to demo.flagd.json setting it off'. That would have been a diff changing nothing, against a file already correct, shipped with a confident rationale. Reading the file is what stopped a plausible and worthless patch.

detail: Read-only probes of the flagd control API at 10.10.1.141:4001. GET /status/productCatalogFailure -> {'ok':true,'defaultVariant':'off',...}. GET /list -> all 15 flags, same reduced shape. POST /ofrep/v1/evaluate/flags/productCatalogFailure -> {'ok':false,'error':'unknown route. Use /toggle/<flag>/<on|off>, /status/<flag>, or /list'}.
finding: Live evaluated state is not readable. The control API exposes only static manifest fields; its one live-state route is /toggle, which this capability may never call (hard rule). So 'the flag is on' is an inference from trace evidence, not a reading - recorded as such in the proposal rather than asserted.
hard_rule_check: No /toggle call made. Read-only throughout. 10.10.1.141 is not 10.10.1.21 (production).

detail: Wrote proposed-change.md + rationale.md to sre-engineer/remediations/inc-001/ (the local audit trail, independent of PR success). v0 proposed a single call: POST /toggle/productCatalogFailure/off, described as restoring the committed upstream definition.

brief: Given only the proposed change and the verified RCA (root cause, implicated file/function). Explicitly NOT given rationale.md or any of my reasoning. Asked the two required questions: does it plausibly address the cited cause, and does it do anything reckless.
verdict_text: The committed targeting block returns 'off' in both branches and would take precedence over defaultVariant in flagd, so the live manifest must have diverged in targeting, which the proposed /toggle/<flag>/off (a defaultVariant selector) cannot reach - the fix may silently no-op, and the proposal's claim that it 'restores the committed definition' is not supportable.
assessment: Correct, and it was the sentence the whole proposal rested on. Worse: I had both halves of the evidence and filed one in the wrong place - I noted the both-branches-'off' targeting rule, and separately noted all 10 product IDs failing against a flag claiming 'a specific product', but listed the second under 'secondary observations, not remediated' as a curiosity about blast radius. Together they are direct evidence that targeting is the field that diverged. Two facts, one inference apart, in separate sections. The consequence would not have been a dangerous change but a silent no-op reported as applied - an incident left live while looking remediated.

detail: The one revision the skill allows. Removed the unsupportable 'restores the committed definition' claim; replaced the single call with a read-first two-case procedure (Step 1 read deployed config; Case A toggle when defaultVariant is the injected field, Case B restore the targeting block in the config source when it is not); promoted the all-10-product-IDs mismatch out of secondary observations into the body as primary evidence; corrected the rollback section, which had implied re-injecting the fault was a sensible response to failed verification; added per-product-ID partial success as the signature of a still-live targeting rule.
deviation_from_reviewer: Did not adopt the reviewer's suggested pre/post diff of /status. Kept its substance, changed its mechanism: /status returns only defaultVariant and description with no targeting field (I have the actual response), so that diff could not have exposed the divergence. Adopting it verbatim would have shipped a verification step that silently cannot verify - the same class of error it had just caught.

why_same_reviewer: It is the authority on whether its own objection was actually met, and it had already verified the primary sources independently. A fresh agent would have judged a different document without knowing what defect it was supposed to test for. Told explicitly not to soften because the revision responded to it.
reviewer_verified: Independently confirmed the precedence model against flagd's own documentation (flagd.dev/reference/flag-definitions): targeting wins when it yields a valid variant; null targeting falls back to defaultVariant; invalid variant is erroneous and the SDK returns the code default, which flags_gen.go pins to false, so malformed targeting fails safe. Confirmed Case B's remedy is robust to defaultVariant. Confirmed the no-restart claim (per-request evaluation, nothing cached). Independently re-probed /status and found defaultVariant already 'off' - corroborating the Case B prediction.
non_blocking_notes_adopted: Two, both adopted. (1) I had overcorrected on /status: it cannot show targeting, but it does show defaultVariant, which is the Case A predicate, and it is the only probe reachable without cluster access - so it became Step 0. (2) Step 1 now records the entire productCatalogFailure object rather than two named fields, because the first draft's defect was that the divergence sat in a field nobody thought to check, and a narrow read reproduces that exposure one level down (concretely: a variants remap binding 'off' to true would defeat BOTH cases). Added a 'neither case matches - stop' branch, the null-targeting fallback in Case A, and recording state for faithful rollback.

outcome: Push blocked. `git push` returned 'Destructive command detected - confirm before running' from this environment's command guard, which needs interactive confirmation that an unattended run cannot supply. Two differently-shaped attempts hit the same guard; stopped rather than keep hammering a declined action.
decision: Did not override the guard. Pushing to a shared repository is outward-facing, and silently disabling a safety check to do it unattended is not this capability's call to make. Recorded pr_url: null with a plain-language pr_error, per the skill's explicit instruction that a rejected push must not sink the remediation. Wrote PR-PENDING.md with the exact commands, branch, commit SHA, preserved clone path, and pre-written PR body so it can be finished in two commands.
distinction: pr_url null with pr_error is NOT type 'deferred'. A real, reviewed, evidence-backed change exists and is written down in full; only transport failed. Conflating the two would understate the outcome.
